note: Generated by tools/gen-goldens.ts from src/entities/Disc.ts (the DiscRuntime half; DiscSystem is renderer-only and has no Swift counterpart). Multi-step traces: each holds one runtime across hundreds of fixed 1/120 steps, scripts the state machine mid-flight, and dumps the whole runtime every sixth frame. Everything here is reachable from + - * / sqrt min max clamp plus the flight integration, so the consuming suite asserts bit-equality except where it states otherwise.

traces.name: backhand-then-catch
traces.note: Held for twelve frames, released as a backhand, flown for two seconds, then caught with hold() and held for twelve more. Exercises the held branch of step(), the trail being cleared at release and again at the catch, sinceRelease resetting, and predictPath called from the middle of a live flight.

traces.name: hammer-blocked-to-ground
traces.note: A left-handed hammer into a cross-wind over sloped ground, knocked down at frame 120 with settle(). A block is settle() plus the game changing possession; the runtime half is the settle. Note settle() does NOT clear the trail, which is what leaves a ribbon hanging behind a swatted disc.

traces.name: push-lands-and-rests
traces.note: A low dump that reaches the grass under its own power and comes to rest. The trail must keep decaying after the disc stops, sinceRelease must keep climbing, and the first frame with touchedGround is where the game stamps a scuff.

traces.name: pull-out-of-bounds
traces.note: A 30 m/s pull with the speed override, aimed across the +x sideline. Records the exact frame the disc leaves the field rectangle and the boundary crossing of the two straddling positions, which is how the game turns a flight into a turnover.

traces.name: scoober-left-handed
traces.note: A left-handed scoober over sloped ground with a small trail budget, so the ring buffer both ages samples out and hits its capacity. predictPath is sampled three times across the flight and once after the disc is on the grass, which is the branch where the caller-supplied pos/vel takes over.

traces.name: pathological-release-parks
traces.note: The module claims a non-finite state "can only come from a pathological release" and is parked rather than poisoning consumers. Asserted as behaviour: the velocity is poisoned mid-flight and the very next step must leave the disc at rest, on the ground, at x = z = 0 and y = groundY + halfHeight.
